brief: An original, instrumental-first polyrhythmic djent album in the tradition of extended-range progressive metal (8-string in F standard, chugging polymeter over a steady 4/4 pulse), but entirely its own music: invent the riffs, rhythms, harmonies and forms; never copy or closely imitate an existing song, including the Meshuggah records we reproduce. One album: a shared tuning, sound world and motif bank that recurs and develops across the tracks, while each track has its own character (tempo, meter, texture, intensity). The songs bleed into one another: no gaps, each ending sets up the next opening. Harsh vocals (the kidman patch) are optional; use them sparingly if at all.
palette: 8-string rhythm guitars m8-emg-l / m8-emg-r (or other m8 variants), leads m8-lead, cleans m8-clean / m8-twang-chorus, bass bass-fat / m8-bass, drums metal-kit-dry (obzen-kit-dry for a brighter kit), pads and textures juno-pad / pad-glass / pad, optional vocals kidman. Tempos anywhere from 60 to 220 BPM. Master each song with a top-level ceiling (-0.1dB).
art_brief: Dark, geometric, mechanical-organic imagery: interlocking gears or lattices dissolving into something living; deep blacks with one cold metallic accent colour.

tracks.brief: The opening. State the album's core motif (a short rhythmic cell plus an interval or harmonic colour) quietly: clean or ambient guitars, pads, distant percussion. Build tension toward the first song; the last seconds bleed straight into track 2.
The statement. Full-force polymetric chug riffing over a steady 4/4 kit pulse; introduce the album's main riff language; high intensity with one release section.
The groove. Mid-tempo, heavy, syncopated, with space and swing in the riffs; a hypnotic figure that slowly mutates. Medium intensity.
The onslaught. The fastest, most frantic track: blast beats, dissonant clusters, short stabbing riffs, abrupt stops. Maximum intensity.
The breath. Mostly clean and atmospheric (clean guitars, pads, a lead melody), a slow or floating feel, with one crushing heavy passage to keep the album's weight. The lowest intensity on the album.
The machine. The odd-meter centrepiece: a long polyrhythmic cycle (for example a phrase of 13 or 23 sixteenths against 4/4) that realigns at section boundaries; mechanical, precise, building.
The ascent. Melodic and soaring: dissonant, lyrical lead guitar over a churning low riff; an emotional climax build; reprise a motif from track 1 or 2, transformed.
The epic closer in several movements: slow-building, reprising and developing motifs from across the album, a crushing peak, and a long ambient dissolve to silence.
